newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Northwest board approves BPA power sales plan.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Northwest board approves BPA power sales plan.

text.p: The Northwest Energy Review Transition Board said Tuesday it approved a plan by the Bonneville Power Administration (BPA) to sell limited amounts of firm power in response to requests from customer utilities that have been approached by other suppliers.

In response to increasing competition in the electricity business, BPA developed a marketing plan to respond to customer utilities that want to make long-term commitments now to buy BPA's power after 2001, when current contracts expire.
Bonneville markets power produced at U.S. Northwest hydroelectric dams and one nuclear plant.
BPA has proposed offering up to 800 megawatts (MW) for sale to Northwest public utilities and industries, but the Transition Board asked that the amount be limited to 500 MW.
The four-member Transition Board was appointed by the governors of Idaho, Montana, Oregon and Washington.

Paul Norman, vice president of generation services for Bonneville, conceded the agency was taking a risk by locking in power sales, but said it seemed likely the market price of power after 2001 will be slightly lower than the current price, according to a Northwest Power Planning Council review of Tuesday's decision.
